generatedProse.concept-context: In sport, you meet experience in coaching placements, work with teams, and practical sessions where you lead or analyse performance. Reflective practice means taking each of these through the cycle, not just noting that the session happened. After a coaching session that did not go to plan, you look back honestly, link it to principles from your course, and decide what you will change in the next session.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students complete the same coaching placement with a junior team. One writes a neat account of the drills they ran and the sessions they led, and leaves it there. The other reflects honestly on a session where the players lost focus, links it to what they had learned about managing attention, and sets out how they will structure the warm-up differently. Over the placement, the second student's accounts show clear insight, because reflection became a practice they kept repeating.
generatedProse.summary: In sport, reflecting on experience becomes one continuing practice across your placements, coaching work and practical sessions. You run the cycle on each, reflect honestly, and articulate what you learned, so one session feeds into the next. It is the habit, not any single account, that turns your practical experience into learning you can show.

check.body: A student finishes a placement, takes it through Kolb's cycle, reflects honestly on a session that went wrong, and writes an account showing what they now do differently. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands worked as one practice: the model, the reflection and the articulation together turned the placement into learning they can show.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three parts ran together on one experience, which is the whole practice.

_items.text: That only the parts of the placement that went wrong are worth reflecting on.
_items.feedback: Honest reflection covers what went well too, not only what went wrong.

_items.text: That the account is strong because it describes the placement in full detail.
_items.feedback: Description alone is not the point. The strength is the evidenced insight, not the detail of events.

_items.text: That the experience alone, once finished, counts as the learning.
_items.feedback: The experience is the occasion. The learning is what the student did with it through the practice.
